claim_boundary.approved_claim: One pinned WebGoat IDOR execution pair is source-bound to one deterministic static scanner observation.

decision_contract.blocked: Use only when the assigned provider or requested review path is unavailable; do not infer a technical defect from unavailability.
decision_contract.go: Use only when the supplied evidence and assigned review scope reveal no material defect in source binding, fail-closed behavior, repeatability, or the stated claim boundary.
decision_contract.hold: Use when a material defect, unproven premise, false-pass path, or claim-boundary violation remains.

implementation_contract.detector: The narrow Spring observer requires a mutating route, a path-variable target, request-body identity distinct from authenticated identity, persistence, and no visible delegated-role or ownership policy. Its medium confidence remains manual-review only.
implementation_contract.observer: The observer validates the complete pinned source workspace and two pre-existing execution receipts, binds integration and implementation route markers, scans the implementation twice, and fails closed on identity, location, receipt, finding-shape, or repeat mismatch.
implementation_contract.parser_fix: Java/Kotlin brace matching now ignores quote and brace characters inside line and block comments before identifying a method body.

review_questions: Does the implementation prove the stated narrow source-to-scanner mapping without silently accepting a changed, partial, or inconsistent source or receipt?
Does the parser fix address the observed comment-handling failure without weakening the existing detector contract?
Do the tests and two identical raw-free mapping receipts support repeatability for this exact narrow field?
Are the explicit nonclaims sufficient so this field cannot be represented as scanner accuracy, TP/FP/FN, L2 completion, or release approval?
